newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Prairie deep freeze to last until Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Canada Prairie deep freeze to last until Wednesday.

text.p: A cold snap ushered in after last Sunday's blizzard across the Canadian Prairies was forecast to last through to Wednesday, November 27, an Environment Canada meteorologist said.

"We're running 15 degrees (Celsius) below normal and this ridge of high pressure will stay over Alberta through the weekend and moves into Manitoba by Wednesday," meteorologist Heather Routledge said.
Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba recorded highs on Thursday between -17 C (1.4 F) and -22 C (-7.6 F) compared to the normal seasonal highs of -1 Celsius (30.2 F).
Snowfall across the Prairies averaged 65 cm (26 inches).
Normal accumulations since October 1 to now are 15 cm (six inches).
"It's typically mid-January temperatures and we have the kind of snow coverage for that time of year across the Prairies as well," Routledge said.

The early and heavy snowfall, with a full month to go before the winter solstice December 21, stopped the harvest in the western Prairies with four percent of grains and oilseeds still left in the field, Agriculture Canada said.
United Grain Growers said 5.0 percent of crops were not harvested in Saskatchewan or Alberta, 3.0 percent in Manitoba.
Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale has approved emergency funds for those farmers with unharvested, damp or tough grain.
Farmers across the Prairies were staying off highways in part because of poor road conditions and overnight lows as cold as -44 Celsius (-47.2 F), grain brokers said.
Snowfall and white-out conditions closed some roads on Canada's Pacific Coast earlier this week and more snow was forecast to fall Saturday.
